current_answer: Google Start offers eligible pre-funded startups up to USD 2,000 in Cloud credits for 12 months, but the credited Billing ID and payment setup matter. In India, some payment methods require a real one-time Postpay prepayment. Google says qualified India organisations using UPI typically needs INR 500–1,000; a temporary card authorization is different. Check the account status and payment type before paying. Neither payment nor a Billing ID guarantees programme approval.

catalogue_card.question: Is that INR 1,000 Google Cloud prompt a refundable hold?
catalogue_card.text: Not necessarily. Google says qualified India organisations using UPI typically needs an INR 500–1,000 prepayment; a card authorization is a different, temporary hold. Google Start credits attach to the Billing ID you submit only if approved. Check the Billing Payment overview before paying.

summary: Google Start lists up to USD 2,000 in Cloud credits for 12 months and asks for an 18-character Billing ID; approval is discretionary.
Some Postpay accounts require a one-time prepayment. Google says qualified India organisations using UPI typically prepay INR 500–1,000; unused Postpay prepayment is refundable at closure.
A temporary card authorization is not an actual charge. An India billing account also needs identity verification within 30 days.
uncertainty: The account-specific INR 1,000 prompt, billing status, payment type and award are unknown without the applicant’s console.
A payment does not prove Start eligibility or guarantee approval.
Other catalogue entries retain their dated verification limits.
